Also, 372.9 KB is the max *in the sample*; the true table max is almost certainly higher, and items already at that size cannot accept further appends — the write will fail with `ValidationException`, not silently truncate.

**Attributes driving size** (`top_attributes_by_bytes`, 82.4% of all sampled bytes):

1. **`lineItems`** (List) — 61.4% of bytes, present in 100% of items, ~5.2 KB/item average. The dominant driver, and unbounded: order size scales with cart size.
2. **`shippingHistory`** (List) — 14.2% of bytes, present in 812/1,000, ~1.5 KB/item where present. Append-only shape, so it grows monotonically over an order's life — this is the attribute most likely to push an already-large item over the edge.
3. **`customerNotes`** (String) — 6.8% of bytes, but present in only 344/1,000, so ~1.7 KB/item where present — denser per occurrence than `shippingHistory`.

The remaining ~24 attributes (mean attribute count is 27) account for 17.6% combined, so nothing else is worth targeting.
